From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Note on scope:** The Seller's package labels some clauses "[STANDARD]" and says they are already cleared. Nothing in the record shows the Buyer has agreed to that, so I have reviewed all 16 items. Figures are from the Seller's documents. Statutory and market points are general and should be confirmed by NSW counsel before the mark-up goes out.

---

## Limitation package

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of at least 30% (AUD 7.2m), with fundamental and tax warranties capped at the full price and fraud uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A 20% cap leaves the Buyer exposed to a large share of the price on a single warranty breach, especially given the open debt, IP and privacy items.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim. AUD 250,000 basket, recoverable only above the basket (deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of AUD 10,000 with related claims aggregated. A tipping basket, so that once it is exceeded the whole amount is recoverable. Basket and de minimis should not apply to fundamental, tax, or specific-indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. A deductible basket of AUD 250,000 would absorb most realistic warranty losses, and the Seller's structure favours the Seller.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general warranty claims, and all limitations apply to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties. Tax claims run until 60 days after the ATO amendment period closes. Fundamental claims run for 6 years, in line with the NSW contract limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. 18 months is short for a business with open privacy, IP and tax questions that may not surface until after the first audit cycle.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, title, authority, and share ownership) uncapped up to the full price, with a 6-year claims period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title is the core of what the Buyer is paying for, and the Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify subjecting it to a general cap.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that nothing limits liability for fraud, with fraud defined and disclosure or time limits not applying.
- **Recommendation:** Insert. Without an express carve-out, the Seller's drafting would purport to limit claims based on the Seller's own fraud, which is a significant gap.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the entire data room, plus the Accounts and public registers, "without limiting" specific disclosures.
- **Buyer should want:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, with reasonable particularity. No general data room disclosure. Public registers disclosed only to the extent specifically referred to.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A blanket data room disclosure would effectively remove most warranty claims, including on the items already flagged in the letter.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** A pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not affect its rights to claim. Knowledge should be limited to the Buyer's actual knowledge at signing, not constructive or data room knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Buyer has already identified multiple issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006), and this clause would let the Seller argue that known issues cannot be claimed, even where the warranty is breached.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all claims, "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities, each with its own cap, basket, and time limit. Default position is that the general regime does not apply to fundamental, tax, or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The "apply to all unless stated otherwise" drafting inverts the usual structure and would cap specific indemnities at the general cap.

---

## Specific issues

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (30%) of FY26 revenue. No final consent is in the data room, and the conditions in clause 11.3 are unverified.
- **Buyer should want:** Final written Bluefen consent, with conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. If it is not obtained, the Buyer can walk away or a price adjustment or escrow applies. A specific indemnity for losses from the change-control clause.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent. Reasonable endeavours is not enough for a contract representing 30% of revenue.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** Payout letter and security discharge delivered at Completion, with the debt repaid from the price in the funds flow. Under a cash-free, debt-free price, this is a debt item the Seller must bear.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Repayment and discharge must happen at Completion, or the Buyer ends up holding a secured facility with no control over it.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. The disclosure is silent on payroll tax and superannuation.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses, plus employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax at the applicable rate, and superannuation guarantee at 12%), treated as debt-like and deducted from the price. A specific indemnity for any other employee entitlements triggered by the sale.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as debt. Under a debt-free, cash-free deal, Completion-triggered liabilities are the Seller's cost.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment of AUD 180,000. The Seller calls this "adequate."
- **Buyer should want:** Evidence of payment, or payment by the Seller before Completion as a debt item. Confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials. A specific indemnity for IP ownership and infringement claims, outside the general cap and basket. A fundamental-style IP ownership warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the limited indemnity. The Buyer cannot confirm it owns the materials, and a payment-only indemnity does not cover IP title or third-party claims.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material."
- **Buyer should want:** Completed forensic investigation before signing or Completion. Confirmation whether the material is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), and whether the notifiable data breach scheme applies. Specific indemnity for notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party costs, outside the general cap and basket, with an extended claims period. Possible escrow or price adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not material." About 1,240 records of names, emails, roles and activity data is a material privacy question, and the Seller's own letter says whether an unauthorised person accessed the file is unknown.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer should want:** Contracts and terms, showing whether they are terminable, multi-year, or prepaid. Any amounts accrued or committed before Completion treated as debt or working capital. A warranty that no commitments exceed the ordinary course without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Require evidence before accepting the characterisation. The Seller's conclusion is not supported by the disclosure, which says it cannot tell whether each renewal is unavoidable or terminable.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC company extract, PPSR search over the shares, inspection of the original register and share transfers, and a warranty that the shares are free of encumbrances. The register is a Seller document and does not show that the Buyer has verified title.
- **Recommendation:** Verify independently. A Seller-supplied register is the source of the title claim, not proof of title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime," meaning the general cap and time limit.
- **Buyer should want:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the general cap and basket, with a claims period running until 60 days after the ATO amendment period closes. IP warranties at a stronger level than general warranties, given the Ironquay issue.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Tax and IP are not "settled" when the Seller has disclosed open items in both areas.

---

## Summary

| Ref | Issue | Priority | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-001 | General cap | High | Counter at 30% |
| N-002 | De minimis / basket | Medium | Tipping basket, lower de minimis |
| N-003 | Time limit | Medium | 24 months general; fundamental 6 years |
| N-004 | Fundamental/title | High | Uncapped to price, 6 years |
| N-005 | Fraud carve-out | High | Insert express carve-out |
| N-006 | Disclosure scope | High | Reject data room disclosure |
| N-007 | Buyer knowledge | High | Reject; insert pro-sandbagging |
| N-008 | Bluefen | High | Condition precedent |
| N-009 | Riverlark | High | Payout and discharge at Completion |
| N-010 | Bonuses | High | Treat as debt-like |
| N-011 | Ironquay IP | High | Specific IP indemnity, confirmatory assignment |
| N-012 | Privacy incident | High | Forensic review, specific indemnity |
| N-013 | Sandbar | Medium | Obtain contracts, treat accruals as debt |
| N-014 | Category separation | High | Separate regimes per category |
| N-015 | Title verification | High | ASIC and PPSR searches, register inspection |
| N-016 | Tax/IP | High | Pre-Completion tax indemnity |

**Items outside the 16 that the Buyer should also check:** The office lease (DD-007) may require landlord consent to the share sale, and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) needs confirmation of whether consent is required. Both should be verified before signing.
